adsbx.acas_ra: A resolution advisory message from the collision avoidance system (TCAS/ACAS), stored as raw encoded bytes (base64 of a JSON blob with the advisory type, timestamp, and threat aircraft hex). Almost always empty in our data; ADS-B Exchange calls this experimental and does not document it fully.
adsbx.alert: A flag bit from the transponder saying the crew changed something notable (for example the squawk code). 0 means no alert, 1 means alert is set. Mostly 0 in our data.
adsbx.alt_baro: Barometric altitude in feet, as the aircraft's pressure altimeter reports it. The text "ground" instead of a number when the aircraft reports it is on the ground.
adsbx.alt_geom: Geometric (GPS-based) altitude in feet, instead of pressure-based. Not set for every plot; only present when the aircraft transmits it.
adsbx.baro_rate: Rate of climb or descent in feet per minute, computed from barometric altitude. Negative means descending, positive means climbing.
adsbx.calc_track: Track over ground in degrees, calculated by ADS-B Exchange from consecutive positions rather than taken from the aircraft's own report. Always empty in our data.
adsbx.category: The aircraft's emitter category code from ADS-B, a rough class like A1 (light aircraft) up to A7 (rotorcraft) or similar. Empty string when the aircraft did not transmit a category.
adsbx.dbFlags: A bitfield of flags from ADS-B Exchange's own aircraft database (for example military or PIA/anonymized). Only set for a small fraction of rows; the numbers are bit combinations, not a single meaning.
adsbx.emergency: The emergency or priority status the aircraft is squawking, as text (for example "none"). Empty string when not reported.
adsbx.flight: Callsign as transmitted by the aircraft, padded with trailing spaces to a fixed width. Often empty when the aircraft does not send one.
adsbx.geom_rate: Rate of climb or descent in feet per minute, computed from geometric (GPS) altitude instead of barometric. Negative means descending.
adsbx.gpsOkBefore: A Unix timestamp (seconds) marking when the aircraft's GPS was last known to be working well, used before that time. Experimental field from ADS-B Exchange, rarely set (about 1% of rows here).
adsbx.gpsOkLat: Latitude of the aircraft's last good GPS position, used while current GPS is considered unreliable. Experimental and rarely set.
adsbx.gpsOkLon: Longitude of the aircraft's last good GPS position, used while current GPS is considered unreliable. Experimental and rarely set.
adsbx.gva: Geometric vertical accuracy, a small integer code (0-2) for how accurate the GPS altitude is expected to be. Higher is more accurate.
adsbx.hex: The aircraft's ICAO 24-bit address in hex, lowercase here. This is the raw ADS-B Exchange field; the normalized, uppercase version used across sources is common.adshex.
adsbx.ias: Indicated airspeed in knots, the speed shown on the aircraft's own airspeed indicator (not corrected for altitude or temperature).
adsbx.mach: Speed as a fraction of the speed of sound (Mach number). Only set at higher altitudes/speeds where the aircraft transmits it.
adsbx.mag_heading: Heading in degrees, measured clockwise from magnetic north. This is where the nose points, not necessarily the direction of travel.
adsbx.messages: Running count of how many Mode S messages ADS-B Exchange has received from this aircraft so far. Grows over time for the same aircraft, so it is more a receiver stat than a per-position value.
adsbx.mlat: List of which fields on this row were derived from MLAT (multilateration, timing-based positioning from multiple ground receivers) rather than direct ADS-B. Empty list means none were MLAT-derived.
adsbx.nac_p: Navigation Accuracy Category for Position, a small integer code. Higher numbers mean the aircraft's own estimate of its position is more accurate.
adsbx.nac_v: Navigation Accuracy Category for Velocity, a small integer code. Higher numbers mean the aircraft's own estimate of its speed/heading is more accurate.
adsbx.nav_altitude_fms: The altitude selected in the aircraft's Flight Management System (the flight plan / route computer), in feet. This is what the aircraft is set to fly to, not its current altitude.
adsbx.nav_altitude_mcp: The altitude selected on the aircraft's Mode Control Panel (the autopilot altitude dial), in feet. This is what the pilot dialed in, not the current altitude.
adsbx.nav_heading: The heading selected by the pilot or autopilot, in degrees. This is a target, not the aircraft's current heading.
adsbx.nav_modes: List of autopilot/automation modes currently engaged, for example autopilot, vnav, lnav, althold, tcas. Empty list means no modes reported as engaged.
adsbx.nav_qnh: The altimeter pressure setting (QNH) the pilot has dialed in, in hectopascals/millibars. Standard sea-level pressure is 1013.25.
adsbx.nic: Navigation Integrity Category, a small integer code for how much to trust the reported position (relates to the containment radius). Higher is better; ties to the rc field.
adsbx.nic_baro: A single bit saying whether the barometric altitude's integrity has been cross-checked (1) or not (0).
adsbx.oat: Outside (static) air temperature in degrees Celsius, as measured by the aircraft, not corrected for the speed of the aircraft through the air.
adsbx.position_timestamp: The time of this position, stored here as text as well as in common.position_timestamp, kept only so BigQuery can partition the table by it. Same value as common.position_timestamp.
adsbx.r: Aircraft registration (tail number) pulled from ADS-B Exchange's own aircraft database, not from the live transmission. This is the raw ADS-B Exchange field; the normalized version used across sources is common.tail_number.
adsbx.rc: Radius of containment in meters: the aircraft is very likely (per its own reported integrity) within this radius of the reported position. Smaller is a tighter, more trustworthy fix.
adsbx.response_timestamp: The time ADS-B Exchange's API responded with this data, meant to be compared against seen and seen_pos to work out how stale the data already was when it arrived.
adsbx.roll: Bank angle in degrees. Negative means rolled/banking to the left.
adsbx.rr_lat: A rough, low-precision latitude for the aircraft based on the position of the receiver that heard it, used as a fallback when a real position is not available. Only set for a tiny fraction of rows here.
adsbx.rr_lon: A rough, low-precision longitude for the aircraft based on the position of the receiver that heard it, used as a fallback when a real position is not available. Only set for a tiny fraction of rows here.
adsbx.rssi: Recent average signal strength of the aircraft's transmissions, in dBFS (decibels relative to full scale, a receiver-side unit). More negative is weaker; not a measure of the aircraft itself.
adsbx.sda: System Design Assurance, a small integer code for how reliable the aircraft's transmitting equipment is designed to be (relates to failure probability, not measurement accuracy).
adsbx.seen: How many seconds before this message was received the aircraft's transponder was last heard from at all (any message, not just position). Small numbers mean fresh data.
adsbx.seen_pos: How many seconds before "now" the position was last updated. Small numbers mean a fresh position.
adsbx.sil: Source Integrity Level, a small integer code for how likely the reported position is wrong beyond what NIC/NAC describe (an error-rate class for the whole system, not just the current fix).
adsbx.sil_type: How to interpret the sil value: per hour, per sample, or unknown. Tells you whether sil is a per-hour or per-message probability.
adsbx.spi: A flag bit meaning the pilot has pressed "ident" (Special Position Identification), used to highlight the aircraft for air traffic control. 1 means ident is active, 0 means not.
adsbx.squawk: The 4-digit transponder code (Mode A/squawk) as text, kept as octal digits like a dial code rather than a number. Empty string when not reported.
adsbx.t: Aircraft type designator (for example B738, A320) pulled from ADS-B Exchange's own aircraft database, not from the live transmission. Duplicates common.ac_type.
adsbx.tas: True airspeed in knots: airspeed corrected for altitude and temperature, closer to the aircraft's real speed through the air than indicated airspeed.
adsbx.tat: Total air temperature in degrees Celsius: outside temperature including the heating effect of the aircraft's own speed through the air. Will read higher than oat, especially at high speed.
adsbx.tisb: List of which fields on this row came from TIS-B (Traffic Information Service-Broadcast, a ground-relayed feed for aircraft without their own ADS-B Out) rather than direct ADS-B. Empty list means none were TIS-B-derived.
adsbx.track: True track over ground in degrees: the direction the aircraft is actually moving, as opposed to where its nose points (heading). This is the raw ADS-B Exchange field; duplicates common.track_deg.
adsbx.track_rate: How fast the track angle is changing, in degrees per second. Positive/negative indicates turning direction.
adsbx.true_heading: Heading in degrees, measured clockwise from true north (as opposed to mag_heading, which uses magnetic north).
adsbx.type: A numeric code for the kind of message/plot this came from (for example plain ADS-B, MLAT, TIS-B). See the ADSBXPlotType enum in the proto; common.provider_source_type carries the same distinction across the pipeline as this code's ADSBXPlotType name.
adsbx.version: The ADS-B version number the aircraft is using (0, 1, or 2), which affects how some of the accuracy fields like nic and sil should be interpreted.
adsbx.wd: Wind direction in degrees, estimated by the aircraft from its own sensors (comparing airspeed/heading to ground speed/track). Not a ground weather station reading.
adsbx.ws: Wind speed in knots, estimated by the aircraft from its own sensors (comparing airspeed/heading to ground speed/track). Not a ground weather station reading.
adsbx.common.ac_type: ICAO aircraft type designator (for example B738), normalized (uppercased/validated) version shared across all sources. For ADS-B Exchange this is the same value as t.
adsbx.common.adshex: The aircraft's ICAO 24-bit address in hex, normalized to uppercase. Same aircraft as hex, just normalized; ADS-B Exchange does not use the non-ICAO '~' prefix convention here so it is never stripped to empty for this source.
adsbx.common.altitude_ft: Altitude in feet, the pipeline's shared altitude field across all sources. For ADS-B Exchange this comes from alt_baro (barometric pressure altitude): the text "ground" becomes 0, and a raw value of -1 becomes unset. Because it is a pressure altitude, it is not corrected to true mean sea level.
adsbx.common.asi_received_timestamp: Unix epoch microseconds, when Air Space Intelligence's integration first parsed this plot into structured data. Use this, not the upstream timestamps, to measure how fast our own pipeline processed it.
adsbx.common.callsign: Aircraft callsign, normalized (whitespace stripped, uppercased) version shared across all sources. For ADS-B Exchange this comes from flight with the padding removed. Empty when the aircraft did not transmit one.
adsbx.common.ground_speed_kt: Ground speed in knots, the pipeline's shared field across all sources. For ADS-B Exchange this is the same value as gs.
adsbx.common.latitude: WGS84 latitude in decimal degrees, range -90 to 90. The shared position field used across all sources, same value as the raw lat this source sends.
adsbx.common.longitude: WGS84 longitude in decimal degrees, range -180 to 180. The shared position field used across all sources, same value as the raw lon this source sends.
adsbx.common.position_timestamp: Unix epoch microseconds: the time the aircraft was actually at this position, as reported by ADS-B Exchange. Same underlying time as the top-level position_timestamp field, just as microseconds instead of text.
adsbx.common.source_identifier: Which upstream data source produced this plot, as a numeric enum code. Always 4 in this table, which is the ADSBX code, since this file only contains ADS-B Exchange plots.
adsbx.common.source_received_timestamp: Unix epoch microseconds meant to capture when the upstream system received the position. ADS-B Exchange does not expose this separately, so the integration just copies position_timestamp into it here; do not use it to estimate upstream-to-ASI lag for this source.
adsbx.common.squawk: 4-digit octal Mode A transponder code, shared field across all sources. For ADS-B Exchange this is the same value as squawk.
adsbx.common.tail_number: Aircraft registration/tail number (for example N12345), normalized version shared across all sources. For ADS-B Exchange this comes from r. Empty when not known.
adsbx.common.track_identifier: The identifier ADS-B Exchange plots use to uniquely track one aircraft: normally the same as hex (uppercased). If an address is one of a small set of known non-unique addresses, it gets a coarse position and hour bucket appended so different aircraft sharing that address do not collide.
adsbx.lastPosition.lat: Latitude of the aircraft's last known position, only filled in when the current position report is stale (last update more than 60 seconds ago). Rare in our data (about 0.03% of rows).
adsbx.lastPosition.lon: Longitude of the aircraft's last known position, only filled in when the current position report is stale (last update more than 60 seconds ago). Rare in our data (about 0.03% of rows).
adsbx.lastPosition.nic: Navigation Integrity Category (see nic) for the aircraft's last known (stale) position, not the current one. Only set alongside the other lastPosition fields.
adsbx.lastPosition.rc: Radius of containment in meters (see rc) for the aircraft's last known (stale) position, not the current one. Only set alongside the other lastPosition fields.
adsbx.lastPosition.seen_pos: How many seconds ago the aircraft's last known (stale) position was updated, at the time that stale snapshot was taken. Values here are large (hundreds to tens of thousands of seconds), unlike the top-level seen_pos, because this only appears once a position has already gone stale.
adsbx.lastPosition: The last-known-position sub-record itself, only present when the aircraft's current position is older than 60 seconds. Always empty in our data (all cases here have fresh positions), so its lat/lon/nic/rc/seen_pos sub-fields never appear as a nested value.

asa.actual_wind: This is the wind as Alaska reports it, direction and speed packed together as digits, for example 278051 meaning 278 degrees at 051 knots. The parsed wind_direction and wind_speed fields split this apart.
asa.air_temperature: This is the outside air temperature in Celsius, parsed from static_air_temp. A negative value comes from an M prefix on the raw field, so M46 becomes -46.
asa.aircraft_registration: This is the aircraft's registration number, like N948AK, exactly as Alaska sent it, before common.tail_number cleans it up.
asa.calibrated_air_speed: This is calibrated airspeed as Alaska sends it, with a K on the end, for example 261K. The parsed calibrated_air_speed_kt field strips the K.
asa.calibrated_air_speed_kt: This is calibrated airspeed in knots, parsed from calibrated_air_speed by removing the K.
asa.current_time: This is the time the ground system logged the ACARS message, shown as a date and time. It is used as the base date for the more precise system_time field.
asa.downlink_stimulus_number: This is a code identifying what triggered the aircraft to send this downlink message. Unclear: what the individual code values mean, we only know it looks like a hex identifier. In our data the raw value has a trailing newline character.
asa.eta_at_goto_waypoint: This is the estimated arrival time at the next waypoint, written as an HHMMSS time of day.
asa.eta_at_goto_waypoint_ts: This is the same estimated arrival time as eta_at_goto_waypoint, converted into a full date and time.
asa.flight_number: This is the flight number Alaska uses, like 365.
asa.following_goto_waypoint_id: This is the identifier of the waypoint after the next one, like KU78M.
asa.fuel_data_update_ts: This is meant to hold when the fuel figure was last updated, taken from a timestamp suffix on the raw fuel message. It is empty in every row we have because that suffix is not present in this data.
asa.goto_waypoint_id: This is the identifier of the next waypoint the aircraft is heading to, like PDT.
asa.ground_speed: This is ground speed in knots, written as a plain number with no letter on the end.
asa.icao_airline_code: This is the 3-letter airline code, ASA for Alaska. It is constant here because every row is an Alaska flight.
asa.icao_departure_airport: This is the departure airport's 4-letter ICAO code, like KAUS.
asa.last_waypoint: This is the identifier of the last waypoint the aircraft passed, like SJT01.
asa.message_time: This is the ACARS message's own timestamp, shown as a date and time. Unclear: exactly how it differs from current_time in practice, since both come from the same message.
asa.position_timestamp: This is the time the aircraft was at this position, shown as a date and time. It is built by combining current_time's date with the more precise system_time.
asa.present_altitude: This is the flight level Alaska's FMC reports, so 360 means flight level 360, roughly 36000 feet. Multiply by 100 to get feet, which is exactly how common.altitude_ft is worked out.
asa.present_position: This is the raw position string Alaska sends, like POSN38413W105503. It packs latitude and longitude together as degrees and minutes; common.latitude and common.longitude are worked out from it.
asa.raw_position_report: This is the full, unparsed ACARS position report line Alaska sent, with every field still packed together and separated by commas. Every other ASA field on this row is pulled out of this one string, and in our data it ends with a trailing newline character.
asa.scheduled_departure_time: This is the flight's scheduled departure date and time.
asa.scheduled_departure_time_ts: This is the same scheduled departure time as scheduled_departure_time, converted into a full date and time. Worth knowing: the parsing code only fills this in when eta_at_goto_waypoint is also present, which looks like a quirk rather than a deliberate rule.
asa.static_air_temp: This is the outside air temperature as Alaska's FMC reports it, for example M46 for minus 46 degrees Celsius. The parsed air_temperature field turns this into a plain number.
asa.system_time: This is the FMC's own clock time for the position report, written as an HHMMSS time of day. It is combined with current_time's date to build the full position_timestamp.
asa.total_fuel: This is the fuel on board in hundreds of pounds, so 186 means 18600 pounds. The parsed total_fuel_lbs field already does that multiplication.
asa.total_fuel_lbs: This is fuel on board in pounds, parsed from total_fuel by multiplying by 100.
asa.true_air_speed: This is true airspeed as Alaska sends it, with a K on the end, for example 456K. The parsed true_air_speed_kt field strips the K.
asa.true_air_speed_kt: This is true airspeed in knots, parsed from true_air_speed by removing the K.
asa.wind_direction: This is wind direction in degrees, parsed from the first 3 digits of actual_wind.
asa.wind_speed: This is wind speed in knots, parsed from the digits after the direction in actual_wind.
asa.common.ac_type: This holds the aircraft type code, like B738. It is always empty here because neither Alaska nor United sends aircraft type.
asa.common.adshex: This is the ICAO 24-bit address in hex, like A12345. It is always empty here because neither Alaska nor United sends this address.
asa.common.altitude_ft: This is altitude in feet. For United it comes from the flight level times 100, and for Alaska it comes from present_altitude times 100. Both are pressure altitude, not height above the ground.
asa.common.asi_received_timestamp: This is the time our system parsed the message, shown as a date and time. It is set automatically when the integration receives the message, not sent by the airline.
asa.common.callsign: This is the flight callsign, like UAL1960. United builds it from the airline code and flight number, but Alaska never fills it in, so it is always empty for Alaska.
asa.common.ground_speed_kt: This is ground speed in knots. For United it only has a value on 4 of the 15 rows here because the source speed field is optional and often missing.
asa.common.latitude: This is the aircraft's latitude in decimal degrees, worked out from the raw position string the airline sent.
asa.common.longitude: This is the aircraft's longitude in decimal degrees, worked out from the raw position string the airline sent.
asa.common.position_timestamp: This is the time the aircraft was at this position, shown as a date and time. For United it comes from source_timestamp; for Alaska it is built from current_time's date and the more precise system_time.
asa.common.source_identifier: This is a fixed code identifying the source. It never changes within one source's data, since each source only ever reports its own code.
asa.common.source_received_timestamp: This is when the upstream system logged the message, shown as a date and time. For United it comes from report_datetime; for Alaska it comes from current_time.
asa.common.squawk: This is the 4-digit transponder code. It is always empty here because neither Alaska nor United sends a squawk code.
asa.common.tail_number: This is the aircraft's registration number, like N58101, cleaned up into a standard format.
asa.common.track_identifier: This is the ID used to tell aircraft apart within one source. For both United and Alaska it is just the raw tail number, before the cleanup that common.tail_number applies.

fused.created_at: The time this event was produced, in microseconds since 1970. For a strategy in this harness this is the raw plot's receipt time, the moment the harness fed the plot in; for production fusion it is when uni-track-fusion actually emitted the event.
fused.quality: One of APPEND_ONLY, REGULAR or RECORRELATION, saying how the event was produced. Every strategy in this harness (baseline and kalman) only ever emits APPEND_ONLY, since they only add plots and never rewrite the past. Production also uses REGULAR after later rewrites and RECORRELATION after a recorrelation.
fused.since: The earliest position time covered by this event's segment, in microseconds since 1970. In practice this always equals until here: baseline and kalman each publish one plot per event, and the harness's production conversion also gives one position time per row. Only a genuine rewrite spanning several plots, which nothing in this harness currently produces, would make since earlier than until.
fused.until: The latest position time covered by this event's segment, in microseconds since 1970. In practice this always equals since here, for the same reason (see since).
fused.longitude: Longitude of the fused plot in decimal degrees, WGS84, from -180 to 180.
fused.latitude: Latitude of the fused plot in decimal degrees, WGS84, from -90 to 90.
fused.position_timestamp: The time the aircraft was actually at this position, in microseconds since 1970, as reported by the source. This is the timestamp used throughout the harness to order plots and to match a raw plot to the fused plot it produced.
fused.source_received_timestamp: When the upstream system received or published this position, in microseconds since 1970. Meant to help split total latency into source-to-upstream and upstream-to-ASI legs, but several sources (ADSBX, PlaneFinder, STDDS, uAvionix) do not really provide this value and it is just copied from position_timestamp for them. Unclear: for any source not listed in the proto comment, check that source's integration before trusting this field for latency numbers.
fused.asi_received_timestamp: When ASI's own source integration first parsed the upstream message into structured form, in microseconds since 1970. Every source integration sets this at parse time, so it is the one timestamp that is reliably the moment ASI first had the plot.
fused.source_identifier: A numeric code for the upstream source that produced this plot, for example 4 for ADS-B Exchange or 11 for uAvionix (see the RAW_SOURCES mapping in production.py for the full list). Together with track_identifier it uniquely identifies one object within that source.
fused.provider_source_type: Probably not useful for most sources: most leave it at the default 0, and uni-track-correlation does not read it at all. Where it is set, it is a numeric code for a sub-feed within a source, such as which ADS-B Exchange plot type or PlaneFinder data source it came from; it is informational for analytics only.
fused.track_identifier: The source's own identifier for the tracked object, unique within one source_identifier. How it is built varies by source, for example the ICAO hex address for ADS-B Exchange or a raw tail number for Alaska Airlines. Together with source_identifier this is the key into uni-track-correlation.
fused.altitude_ft: Altitude in feet, as the source itself reports it. What kind of altitude this actually is (barometric, ground height, or geometric) differs by source, so it should be read as the source's own idea of altitude rather than one consistent measurement. Note: uAvionix data pulled before 22 September 2026 had a bug where this field held GPS height instead of barometric altitude; later pulls are fixed (see the harness README).
fused.ground_speed_kt: Ground speed in knots. Only set by sources that report it directly, such as ADS-B Exchange, PlaneFinder and TFMS; other sources vary. Note: uAvionix data pulled before 22 September 2026 had a bug where this was actually in nautical miles per second, not knots; later pulls are fixed (see the harness README).
fused.callsign: The aircraft's callsign, for example AAL1234. Cleaned up (whitespace stripped, uppercased) by a shared library before it lands here. Some sources leave it empty, for example Alaska never sets it and United builds its own from an airline code plus flight number. In production fusion, if the callsign is empty and the plot came from TFMS, fusion fills it in from the FAA flight reference instead; that is the one case where a fused plot's callsign can differ from the raw plot it came from.
fused.tail_number: The aircraft's registration number, for example N12345. Not every source provides it: TFMS, STDDS and uAvionix leave it empty, while ADS-B Exchange, PlaneFinder, Alaska and United fill it in from their own registration field.
fused.adshex: The aircraft's ICAO 24-bit address written in hex, for example A12345. Some feeds mark a non-ICAO address with a leading ~; that prefix gets stripped down to an empty value here, and the original stays on track_identifier instead. Empty for TFMS, Alaska and United, which do not carry this field.
fused.squawk: The 4-digit Mode A transponder code the aircraft is broadcasting, for example 2400. Set by ADS-B Exchange, PlaneFinder, uAvionix and STDDS; empty for TFMS, Alaska and United.
fused.ac_type: The ICAO aircraft type code, for example B738. Empty for sources that do not carry an aircraft type at all: Alaska, United, uAvionix and STDDS.
fused.flight_number: The flight number. Only PlaneFinder puts this on the shared field; sources that do have a flight number, such as Alaska and United, keep it on their own source-specific fields instead of here.
fused.heading_deg: Unclear: whether this is true heading or magnetic heading is not stated on the field itself, and it actually varies by source, for example true heading for ADS-B Exchange but magnetic heading for uAvionix, so values from different sources are not directly comparable. It is the aircraft's compass heading in degrees clockwise, from 0 up to 360; TFMS, Alaska and United do not set it.
fused.track_deg: The aircraft's direction of travel over the ground, in degrees clockwise, true north, from 0 up to 360. For the kalman strategy this is computed from the filter's own velocity estimate rather than copied from a raw plot. In production, some sources cut corners here, for example STDDS just copies its heading value into this field instead of measuring real track; TFMS, Alaska and United do not set it at all.
fused.above_ground_altitude_ft: A deprecated field kept only so older readers of the data still work. New code should read Common.above_ground_altitude_ft instead of this one, and nothing in this harness sets it.
fused.mean_sea_level_altitude_ft: Unclear: despite the name, this mostly just reuses altitude_ft once it is above 0 feet, without correcting for local air pressure (QNH), so it is not a true sea-level altitude while airborne, only close to the ground. It is worked out by uni-track-multiplexer from altitude_ft plus the ground elevation at that point, in feet; no source sets it directly.
fused.flight_ref: FAA TFMS's own flight reference id. Only set when the raw plot came from TFMS; empty for every other source.
fused.selected_altitude_ft: The altitude the aircraft's autopilot or flight management system is set to fly to, in feet, when known. Only PlaneFinder provides this; every other source leaves it unset.
fused.vert_rate_fpm: How fast the aircraft is climbing or descending, in feet per minute. Positive means climbing, negative means descending. Only ever set from PlaneFinder or ADS-B Exchange, and the two are not quite the same measurement: ADS-B Exchange's is confirmed barometric, while PlaneFinder's is not documented and may be geometric.
fused.pressure_hpa: The barometric altimeter setting (QNH) in hectopascals. Only PlaneFinder provides this; unset for every other source.
fused.flight_id: An internal id that uni-track-fusion assigns to link a track over time to a flight plan and its gate, taxi, takeoff and landing events. Only production fusion strategies set this. The harness's own strategies, baseline and kalman, never assign one, so this is always empty for them.
fused.original_callsign: The callsign as it originally came from the source, before fusion's cleanup and, for TFMS, its callsign fallback ran. For every source except PlaneFinder this ends up being the same value as callsign; only PlaneFinder can actually carry something different here.
fused.origin: Probably a mix of ICAO codes (like KJFK) and IATA codes (like JFK), depending on what the flight-plan source provides; this has not been checked and verified. It is the flight's departure airport, filled in by production fusion from a matching flight-plan record, and left empty when no match is found. The harness's own strategies never set it.
fused.destination: Probably has the same ICAO-or-IATA uncertainty as origin, since it is filled in from the same flight-plan record. It is the flight's arrival airport, set by production fusion the same way as origin; the harness's own strategies never set it.
fused.valid_to: Added by the harness itself, not part of the proto. It is the created_at time (microseconds since 1970) of the first later event on the same track whose segment covers this plot's position, meaning the moment this version of the plot stopped being current. Empty if nothing has replaced it yet. The viewer uses this to show only the version of a plot that was actually current at a given moment in the timeline.
fused.sigma_east_m: How far off the filter thinks its east-west position estimate may be, in metres, as one standard deviation. Only the kalman strategy records this, taken from the filter's own uncertainty matrix and rotated into local east, north and up directions.
fused.sigma_north_m: How far off the filter thinks its north-south position estimate may be, in metres, as one standard deviation. Only the kalman strategy records this, the same way as sigma_east_m.
fused.sigma_up_m: How far off the filter thinks its vertical position estimate may be, in metres, as one standard deviation. Only the kalman strategy records this; by the filter's own settings it tends to run larger than the horizontal sigmas (1.5 times, by default).
fused.sigma_speed_mps: How far off the filter thinks its horizontal speed estimate may be, in metres per second, as one standard deviation. It combines the filter's east and north velocity uncertainty into one number. Only the kalman strategy records this.
fused.distance_m: How far a raw plot's reported position actually was from where the kalman filter expected the aircraft to be, in metres, at the moment it was used as a measurement. Only recorded by the kalman strategy, and only on plots it used, not on skipped, dropped or rejected ones.
fused.distance_sigmas: The same gap as distance_m, but measured in standard deviations of the filter's expected uncertainty instead of metres. If the filter's noise assumptions are right, values below about 3 should cover roughly 97 out of 100 plots; a value around 10 means the plot landed far from what the filter believed, a possible sign of a bad measurement or a wrong filter setting.
fused.state: What a strategy did with this raw plot: used (taken as a measurement into a track), skipped (a fixed rule says this kind of plot is never used by this strategy), dropped (the right kind of plot, but its timing made it unusable, for example a duplicate or an out-of-order plot), rejected (checked against a track and refused), or unknown (the strategy recorded nothing about it). Production always reports unknown for a plot it did not use, since it never says why a plot was left out.
fused.track_id: The strategy's track id that this raw plot was matched against, when there is one, for example the ADS-B hex for the kalman strategy. Always empty for a skipped plot, since those are refused before any track is even considered; usually set for used, dropped and rejected plots to say which track was involved.
fused.reason: A short, few-word explanation for why a plot was skipped, dropped or rejected, for example "on the ground" or "out of order". Empty for a used plot, and always empty for production since it never explains why a plot was left out.

planefinder.ac_type: The aircraft's ICAO type code, such as B738 or A320, as PlaneFinder reports it. Copied into common.ac_type.
planefinder.altitude: PlaneFinder's own altitude reading, in feet. The reference is not documented upstream: it reads 0 on the ground but mixes barometric and MSL-like altitude in flight, and in Kielce it jumped by 11,700 ft on several aircraft for stretches of time, so treat sudden large jumps with suspicion.
planefinder.barometer: The barometric pressure setting (QNH) dialed into the aircraft, in hectopascals. Standard sea-level pressure is 1013.25 hPa, which is why most values cluster near 1013.
planefinder.callsign: The flight callsign PlaneFinder reports for this aircraft, cleaned up. Can be empty if PlaneFinder never picked one up.
planefinder.category: The ADS-B emitter category code (like A1 or A3), a standard code for the kind and weight class of the aircraft or vehicle transmitting.
planefinder.data_source: A numeric code for which PlaneFinder signal type produced this plot: 1 is ADS-B, 2 is PlaneFinder's own MLAT, 3 is FLARM (a glider/light-aircraft transponder system), 4 is MLAT computed by someone else and relayed by PlaneFinder, 5 is blocked data.
planefinder.flight_number: The flight number shown for this flight, such as TK3015. Can be empty and often looks similar to the callsign.
planefinder.gs: Ground speed in knots: how fast the aircraft is moving over the ground, ignoring wind.
planefinder.heading: Unclear: the proto only says unit degrees. Since magnetic_heading is a separate field, this is probably true heading, the direction the nose points relative to true north, not the direction of travel over the ground.
planefinder.ias: Indicated air speed in knots: the speed shown on the pilot's own airspeed gauge, read from air pressure and not corrected for altitude.
planefinder.is_blocked: Whether the aircraft's owner asked for this aircraft's data to be hidden. Some private and business aircraft opt out this way.
planefinder.is_on_ground: Whether PlaneFinder believes the aircraft is on the ground, based on the ADS-B surface flag or an MLAT estimate.
planefinder.last_seen_time: The last time PlaneFinder heard anything from this aircraft, in microseconds since the Unix epoch. Can differ slightly from pos_update_time, which is specific to this position.
planefinder.mach: Speed as a fraction of the local speed of sound. A value of 0.78 means the aircraft is flying at 78% of the speed of sound where it currently is.
planefinder.magnetic_heading: The direction the aircraft's nose points, in degrees measured from magnetic north rather than true north.
planefinder.oat: Outside air temperature in Celsius, as measured by the aircraft's own sensor at its current altitude.
planefinder.original_callsign: The callsign as first read, before PlaneFinder's own cleanup. Usually the same as callsign but kept separately in case cleanup changes it.
planefinder.pos_update_time: The time this position was last updated, PlaneFinder's own name for what is elsewhere called the track timestamp. Close to but not guaranteed identical to common.position_timestamp.
planefinder.reg: The aircraft's registration or tail number, such as TC-JRH. Can be empty.
planefinder.roll_angle: The aircraft's bank angle in degrees: how far it is tilted left or right. Zero means wings level.
planefinder.route: The aircraft's route as a string of IATA airport codes joined by hyphens, such as VKO-AYT. Can list more than two airports if the route has stops, and can be empty.
planefinder.selected_altitude: The altitude dialed into the autopilot's altitude window, in feet. This is the target altitude the crew selected, not necessarily the altitude the aircraft is at right now.
planefinder.speed: Probably PlaneFinder's main speed reading for this plot, in knots. PlaneFinder also reports more specific speeds separately (gs, ias, tas); it is unclear exactly how this one relates to those.
planefinder.station_id: An ID for the PlaneFinder ground station that most recently reported this aircraft. Meant for debugging with PlaneFinder, not for analysis.
planefinder.target_heading: The heading dialed into the autopilot's heading selector, in degrees. This is the commanded heading, which may not match the heading the aircraft is actually flying.
planefinder.tas: True air speed in knots: the aircraft's speed through the surrounding air mass, corrected for altitude and temperature. Faster than indicated air speed at high altitude.
planefinder.track_angle: The direction the aircraft is actually moving over the ground, in degrees. This is the flight path (course), which can differ from heading when wind pushes the aircraft sideways.
planefinder.vert_rate: The aircraft's climb or descent rate. The schema gives no unit, but the values are multiples of 64, which matches feet per minute, the usual ADS-B step size. Positive is probably climbing.
planefinder.wind_direction: The direction the wind is blowing from, in degrees, as sensed or computed by the aircraft.
planefinder.wind_speed: Wind speed in knots, as sensed or computed by the aircraft.
planefinder.common.ac_type: The aircraft's ICAO type code (such as B738), as PlaneFinder reports it and after ASI's own normalization step.
planefinder.common.adshex: The aircraft's ICAO 24-bit address in hex, as PlaneFinder reports it. This is the same kind of address other ADS-B sources use, and normally stays fixed for one aircraft.
planefinder.common.altitude_ft: PlaneFinder's altitude reading in feet, copied from the plain altitude field above. The datum mixes barometric and MSL-like altitude and is not documented upstream; watch for the 11,700 ft jumps seen in Kielce on some aircraft.
planefinder.common.asi_received_timestamp: The time, in microseconds since the Unix epoch, when ASI's PlaneFinder integration parsed this message into structured form. This is an ASI-side ingest time, not when the aircraft was actually there.
planefinder.common.callsign: The flight callsign, cleaned up and uppercased by ASI's normalization step. Can be empty if PlaneFinder never provided one.
planefinder.common.ground_speed_kt: Ground speed in knots, as PlaneFinder reports it. Same idea as the gs field above.
planefinder.common.latitude: Latitude in decimal degrees (WGS84), between -90 and 90. PlaneFinder's position comes from the same GPS fix as other ADS-B sources, so for ADS-B plots it usually agrees with them to about a metre; MLAT-derived positions (see data_source) are rougher.
planefinder.common.longitude: Longitude in decimal degrees (WGS84), between -180 and 180. Same accuracy notes as common.latitude apply.
planefinder.common.position_timestamp: The time PlaneFinder says the aircraft was at this position, in microseconds since the Unix epoch. PlaneFinder plots are measured 3.1 seconds late at the median, the offset varies by receiving station from about -0.5 s to +0.1 s, and roughly 7% of plots arrive more than 10 seconds after this time.
planefinder.common.source_identifier: A numeric code identifying PlaneFinder as the source of this plot. The same value for every PlaneFinder row.
planefinder.common.source_received_timestamp: For PlaneFinder this is always set equal to common.position_timestamp, because PlaneFinder does not expose its own upstream-received time. Do not use this field to estimate PlaneFinder's lag; it will always read zero lag.
planefinder.common.squawk: The aircraft's 4-digit octal transponder code (squawk), as PlaneFinder reports it. Can be empty.
planefinder.common.tail_number: The aircraft's registration or tail number, with punctuation stripped, such as TCJRH instead of TC-JRH.
planefinder.common.track_identifier: PlaneFinder's own per-aircraft key for this track, taken from its adshex address (with a fallback re-keying scheme for a small set of known non-unique addresses). Normally stays the same across plots from the same aircraft.

stdds.airport: The four letter ICAO code of the airport this surface radar feed covers. Always KSLC (Salt Lake City) in our data.
stdds.enhanced_data: A group of fields added from the FAA's flight plan system (departure and destination airport, flight IDs). This container itself has no value in the flattened table; look at the enhanced_data.* fields. Always empty here.
stdds.flight_id: A group of fields holding the automatically tracked callsign, radio address, and squawk code. This container itself has no value in the flattened table; look at the flight_id.* fields. Always empty here.
stdds.flight_info: A group of fields holding automatically tracked flight details (aircraft type, exit fix, runway, wake class). This container itself has no value in the flattened table; look at the flight_info.* fields. Always empty here.
stdds.is_full: True if this report is a complete snapshot of the track, false if it only carries the fields that changed since the last report.
stdds.manual: A group of fields entered by hand by an air traffic controller (aircraft type, callsign, wake class, free text notes). This container itself has no value in the flattened table; look at the manual.* fields. Always empty here.
stdds.plot_count: A count from the radar subsystem, probably the number of radar hits used to build this track update. Only set on about 1 in 7 rows in our data; ranges from 0 to 4 when present.
stdds.position_timestamp: The time of this position report, shown as a normal date and time. Same instant as common.position_timestamp, kept as a separate copy so BigQuery can use it to split the table into daily partitions.
stdds.seq_num: A counter that goes up by one each time the airport's surface radar system (ASDE-X or ASSC) sends a message for this track. Used to spot messages that arrived out of order; not a physical measurement.
stdds.slc: A group of internal FAA table index numbers (coast, suspended, and local vehicle list numbers) used inside the radar system. This container itself has no value in the flattened table; look at the slc.* fields. Always empty here.
stdds.status: A group of status flags and quality indicators about how this track was formed (which sensors contributed, alerts, navigation accuracy). This container itself has no value in the flattened table; look at the status.* fields. Always empty here.
stdds.stid: A unique ID number assigned by STDDS (the FAA's system that distributes this data) to this track. FAA note: this ID is not unique across airports or time, so ASI uses the aircraft's radio address instead when it needs a stable ID.
stdds.target_extent: A group of fields describing the size and shape of the radar return (start and end angle and range, an extent estimate), used by the surface radar to judge how big the object is. This container itself has no value in the flattened table; look at the target_extent.* fields. Always empty here.
stdds.time: The time of this position report as text, in the format yyyy-mm-ddThh:mm:ss.sssZ. Same instant as position_timestamp, just written out instead of stored as microseconds.
stdds.track: The track number the surface radar system assigned to this aircraft or vehicle. These numbers get reused for different aircraft over time, so they are not a stable ID; that is why ASI uses the aircraft's radio address (adshex) as the real identifier instead.
stdds.common.above_ground_altitude_ft: Height above the ground in feet. This is worked out later by ASI's own processing (multiplexer service) from altitude and terrain data, not by this source feed, so it is always empty in the raw STDDS data.
stdds.common.ac_type: The aircraft type code (ICAO format, e.g. B738). Taken from the automatically tracked flight info first, and filled in from the manually entered field if the automatic one is missing or invalid. Empty when neither is available.
stdds.common.adshex: The aircraft's ICAO 24 bit radio address, written as 6 hex digits (e.g. A04229). This is the one field STDDS reliably gives that is unique to the aircraft, so ASI also uses it as the track identifier below.
stdds.common.altitude_ft: Altitude in feet, taken directly from the source position.altitude field (FAA calls this mode-C or surface altitude). For STDDS this is a raw reading, not corrected to true mean sea level.
stdds.common.asi_received_timestamp: Unix epoch time in microseconds of when ASI's STDDS integration parsed this message into a structured record, i.e. when ASI first had the data in a usable form.
stdds.common.callsign: The aircraft's callsign, e.g. UAL2740. Taken from the automatically tracked flight ID first, and filled in from the manually entered callsign if the automatic one is missing or invalid. Empty when neither is available.
stdds.common.flight_number: Flight number field shared across all sources. STDDS does not expose a flight number, so this is always empty here.
stdds.common.ground_speed_kt: Ground speed in knots. Comes from the smoothed speed value in the source movement data.
stdds.common.heading_deg: Heading in degrees clockwise from north (0 to 360). Comes from the source's smoothed movement heading; the FAA documentation for STDDS does not say whether this is true or magnetic north, so treat the exact reference as unverified.
stdds.common.latitude: WGS84 latitude in decimal degrees, from -90 to 90.
stdds.common.longitude: WGS84 longitude in decimal degrees, from -180 to 180.
stdds.common.mean_sea_level_altitude_ft: Altitude in feet relative to mean sea level, worked out later by ASI's processing from altitude_ft. Caveat: the formula assumes altitude_ft above 0 is already MSL, which is not strictly true for a pressure based reading like STDDS gives, so treat this as approximate.
stdds.common.position_timestamp: Unix epoch time in microseconds at which the aircraft was at this position, as reported by the source.
stdds.common.provider_source_type: A code for which sub feed or sensor within STDDS produced this plot. STDDS does not set this, so it is always 0 (not set) in our data.
stdds.common.source_identifier: A numeric code for which upstream feed produced this plot. Always 10 in this table, which is the code for STDDS SMES surface position reports.
stdds.common.source_received_timestamp: Unix epoch time in microseconds meant to record when the upstream system received or published this position. STDDS does not expose this separately, so the integration just copies position_timestamp into it; do not use it to estimate delay for this source.
stdds.common.squawk: The 4 digit octal transponder (Mode A/3A) code, e.g. 1200. Taken from the automatically tracked value first, and filled in from the manually entered code if the automatic one is missing or invalid.
stdds.common.tail_number: Aircraft registration / tail number field shared across all sources. STDDS does not expose a tail number, so this is always empty here.
stdds.common.track_deg: Track over the ground in degrees clockwise from north. For STDDS this is not an independent measurement: the integration just copies the heading_deg value into it, so it always equals common.heading_deg.
stdds.common.track_identifier: The ID ASI uses to identify this aircraft within the STDDS feed. Since the FAA's own track ID (stid) is not unique across time, the integration uses the aircraft's ICAO radio address (adshex) here instead.
stdds.movement.ax: Calculated forward/east-west (X) component of the track's acceleration, in meters per second squared.
stdds.movement.ay: Calculated sideways/north-south (Y) component of the track's acceleration, in meters per second squared.
stdds.movement.heading: Smoothed heading of the aircraft or vehicle relative to true north, in degrees. This is the same value copied into common.heading_deg.
stdds.movement.speed: Smoothed speed of the aircraft or vehicle in knots.
stdds.movement.vx: Calculated east-west (X) component of the aircraft's velocity, in meters per second.
stdds.movement.vy: Calculated north-south (Y) component of the aircraft's velocity, in meters per second.
stdds.position.altitude: Altitude in feet above mean sea level of the fused track, as computed by the airport's surface radar system. This is the field common.altitude_ft and position.altitude both come from.
stdds.position.extended_x: X coordinate, in a local Cartesian grid centered on the airport, for aircraft more than 17 nautical miles away. Always empty in our data, since STDDS here only covers traffic close to the airport.
stdds.position.extended_y: Y coordinate, in a local Cartesian grid centered on the airport, for aircraft more than 17 nautical miles away. Always empty in our data, since STDDS here only covers traffic close to the airport.
stdds.position.flight_level: Flight level (altitude in hundreds of feet) reported for the track. Unclear exactly how this differs from position.altitude in the FAA source data; likely another view of the same pressure altitude reading.
stdds.position.latitude: WGS84 latitude in decimal degrees. Same value as common.latitude, just rounded to fewer decimal places in this raw field.
stdds.position.longitude: WGS84 longitude in decimal degrees. Same value as common.longitude, just rounded to fewer decimal places in this raw field.
stdds.position.x: X coordinate of the aircraft in the airport's local Cartesian grid (a flat, meters-like coordinate system centered on the airport), not a latitude/longitude.
stdds.position.y: Y coordinate of the aircraft in the airport's local Cartesian grid (a flat, meters-like coordinate system centered on the airport), not a latitude/longitude.
stdds.enhanced_data.aircraft_type: Aircraft type from the FAA flight plan system. The FAA's STDDS feed does not fill in this field for SMES surface data, so it is always empty here.
stdds.enhanced_data.beacon_code: Transponder beacon code from the FAA flight plan system. The FAA's STDDS feed does not fill in this field for SMES surface data, so it is always empty here.
stdds.enhanced_data.departure_airport: ICAO code of the departure airport, taken from the aircraft's flight plan (not from the radar track itself). Empty when there is no matching flight plan.
stdds.enhanced_data.destination_airport: ICAO code of the destination airport, taken from the aircraft's flight plan (not from the radar track itself). Empty when there is no matching flight plan.
stdds.enhanced_data.eram_gufi: A unique flight identifier (GUFI, Globally Unique Flight Identifier) assigned by ERAM, the FAA's en-route air traffic control computer system. Links this track to a specific flight plan.
stdds.enhanced_data.sfdps_gufi: A unique flight identifier (GUFI) assigned by SFDPS, the FAA's SWIM service that publishes flight plan data. Links this track to a specific flight plan; can be empty even when eram_gufi is set.
stdds.target_extent.end_azimuth: The ending compass angle (bearing from the radar, in degrees) of the radar return used to size this target.
stdds.target_extent.end_range: The ending distance from the radar, in an FAA-defined unit (likely radar range bins, not meters or feet), of the return used to size this target.
stdds.target_extent.estimate: A code from the FAA's Extent field that summarizes how big the radar thinks the target is. Matches the Extent field defined in the ASDE-X and ASSC interface documents; the exact meaning of each number is not documented in our code.
stdds.target_extent.start_azimuth: The starting compass angle (bearing from the radar, in degrees) of the radar return used to size this target.
stdds.target_extent.start_range: The starting distance from the radar, in an FAA-defined unit (likely radar range bins, not meters or feet), of the return used to size this target.
stdds.status.a9s: 1 if the ASR-9 radar (a long range airport surveillance radar) contributed to this track, 0 if not.
stdds.status.aa: 1 if this track is linked to an ADS-B (satellite/GPS based aircraft broadcast) report, 0 if not.
stdds.status.af: Whether an alert on this track is filtered. 0 means not set, 1 means unfiltered (shown), 2 would mean filtered (hidden), 3 would mean highlighted; only 0 and 1 appear in our data.
stdds.status.ap: 1 if the track is coasting (radar temporarily lost it) while parked in an apron/gate area, 0 if not.
stdds.status.aq: 1 if there is a question about whether a coasting track is still correctly associated with this aircraft, 0 if not. Always 0 in our data.
stdds.status.aq1090: Which kind of address the aircraft's 1090 MHz ADS-B (the standard aircraft broadcast frequency) message carried. 0 means not set; the other codes stand for different address types such as ICAO or non-ICAO IDs.
stdds.status.aq_uat: Which kind of address the aircraft's UAT (978 MHz, the ADS-B band mainly used by smaller/general aviation aircraft) message carried. 0 means not set; the other codes stand for different address types.
stdds.status.as: 1 if an ADS-B (satellite/GPS based aircraft broadcast) source was fused into this track, 0 if not.
stdds.status.at: 1 if ATCRBS (the older secondary radar transponder system used with air traffic control radar) contributed to this track, 0 if not. Always 0 in our data.
stdds.status.av: How valid the track's coordinates are, as judged by the radar system: 0 not set, 1 unknown, 2 invalid, 3 reserved, 4 valid.
stdds.status.da: 1 if this aircraft's Mode A transponder code duplicates another aircraft's, 0 if not. Always 0 in our data.
stdds.status.df: 1 if this track duplicates another flight's identity, 0 if not. Always 0 in our data.
stdds.status.di: 1 if this track is flagged to be shown on the controller's display, 0 if not.
stdds.status.gbs: 1 if the aircraft is judged to be airborne (not on the ground), 0 if it is on the ground.
stdds.status.gm: 1 if the GPS reported position is more than 100 feet away from the position the radar worked out by multilateration (triangulating multiple ground sensors), 0 if not. Always 0 in our data.
stdds.status.ls: 1 if support from a sensor was lost while coasting (radar temporarily lost the track), 0 if not.
stdds.status.lv: 1 if this track is linked to the airport's local vehicle list, 0 if not. Always 0 in our data.
stdds.status.lv_1090: A link version number for the 1090 MHz ADS-B (aircraft broadcast) data expansion field. Always 2 in our data.
stdds.status.lv_uat: A link version number for the UAT (978 MHz ADS-B band) data expansion field. Always 2 in our data.
stdds.status.m3c: 1 if the aircraft's Mode 3/A transponder code changed since the last report, 0 if not. Always 0 in our data.
stdds.status.mon: 1 if this track is being tracked by only one sensor (monosensor), 0 if more than one sensor is contributing.
stdds.status.mrh: Whether the reported altitude is barometric (from air pressure) or geometric (from GPS/satellite height): 0 not set, 1 barometric, 2 geometric. Only 0 and 1 appear in our data.
stdds.status.ms: 1 if Mode S (a newer transponder mode that also carries ADS-B and aircraft ID data) was fused into this track, 0 if not. Always 0 in our data.
stdds.status.nacp: Navigation Accuracy Category for position, an FAA/ADS-B code from 0 to 11 where higher means the aircraft's own GPS reports a tighter accuracy bound on its position.
stdds.status.nc: 1 if a multipath, non-cooperative radar return contributed (a return from something without a transponder, possibly a reflection), 0 if not.
stdds.status.nic: Navigation Integrity Category, an FAA/ADS-B code from 0 to 11 where higher means the aircraft's own system reports a smaller guaranteed error radius for its position.
stdds.status.op: 1 if the track is coasting (temporarily lost) during an oscillation/turn period, 0 if not. Always 0 in our data.
stdds.status.quality: Unclear: an FAA track quality score (0 to 15 in our data). Likely a general figure of merit for how good the surface radar considers this track's position estimate, similar to a confidence score, but the exact FAA definition is not in our code.
stdds.status.rt: 1 if this track is a reference transmitter track (a fixed ground beacon used to calibrate the radar, not a real aircraft), 0 if not. Always 0 in our data.
stdds.status.s1: 1 if the 1090 MHz ADS-B (standard aircraft broadcast) source was fused for this track, 0 if not.
stdds.status.si: 1 if safety-alert logic has been turned off for this track, 0 if not. Always 0 in our data.
stdds.status.sil: Source Integrity Level, an FAA/ADS-B code (0 to 3) for how likely the aircraft's own reported position is to be wrong without it knowing. Only 0 and 3 appear in our data.
stdds.status.sim: 1 if this data came from an engineering test/playback session rather than live traffic, 0 if it is live. Always 0 in our data.
stdds.status.spi: 1 if the aircraft's transponder had its Special Position Identification (an ident button press air traffic control asks pilots to make) flag set on the last report, 0 if not. Always 0 in our data.
stdds.status.src: Which sensor type the fused height/altitude came from: 0 not set, 1 none, 2 ADS-B, 3 Mode C, 4 multilateration, 5 ground (on surface), 6 multiple sources.
stdds.status.ss: 1 if the airport's Surface Movement Radar (the ground radar that scans the tarmac and runways) was fused into this track, 0 if not.
stdds.status.st: 1 if this is a suspended track (temporarily set aside by the radar system), 0 if not. Always 0 in our data.
stdds.status.su: 1 if a UAT (978 MHz ADS-B band) source was fused for this track, 0 if not.
stdds.status.tc: 1 if there is a conflict between the manually entered tag and the automatic one for this track, 0 if not. Always 0 in our data.
stdds.status.tf: 1 if a taxiway arrival alert was filtered (suppressed) for this track, 0 if not. Always 0 in our data.
stdds.status.tse: 1 if this was the last message received for this track, 0 if not.
stdds.status.twy_id: A numeric ID for which taxiway the surface radar predicts the aircraft is on. 0 most likely means not on a taxiway or unknown; the mapping from ID number to taxiway name is not in our code.
stdds.status.ua: 1 if a UAT (978 MHz ADS-B band) source was fused for this track, 0 if not. Always 0 in our data.
stdds.status.ud: Direction the vertical rate (climb/descent) is going: 0 not set, 1 up, 2 down.
stdds.status.uncorr_baro_alt: The most recent barometric (air pressure based) altitude the aircraft itself reported, before any correction. Unit is likely feet, consistent with the rest of the altitude fields, though this is not stated explicitly in the source.
stdds.status.vert_rate: Vertical rate of climb or descent for the track. Unit is not stated in the source; direction (up/down) is given separately in status.ud, so this is likely a magnitude in feet per minute.
stdds.status.vs: Whether the vertical rate (climb/descent) was computed from barometric (air pressure) or geometric (GPS/satellite) data: 0 not set, 1 barometric, 2 geometric.
stdds.status.x: 1 if the ATCRBS (older secondary radar transponder) X bit is set, a special FAA status flag whose exact meaning is not documented in our code. Always 0 in our data.
stdds.flight_info.ac_type: Aircraft type in ICAO format (e.g. B738), automatically tracked by the radar system. Shows ANON if the flight is marked anonymized, empty if not known.
stdds.flight_info.fix: Exit fix, usually a three letter navigation point name, for arrival flights, taken from the flight plan. Empty for flights without a matching flight plan.
stdds.flight_info.runway: Name of the departure or arrival runway (e.g. 35, 34L), automatically tracked. Can also contain the words 'filtered' or 'unassigned' instead of a runway name, or be empty.
stdds.flight_info.tgt_type: What kind of object the radar thinks this is: 0 unspecified, 1 unknown, 2 aircraft, 3 vehicle, 4 unknown aircraft.
stdds.flight_info.wake: Wake turbulence category letter for the aircraft (how much wake turbulence it generates, used to space aircraft apart), automatically tracked. Empty when not known.
stdds.flight_id.ac_address: The aircraft's ICAO radio address as six hex digits, automatically tracked from the transponder. Same kind of value as common.adshex.
stdds.flight_id.aircraft_id: Callsign automatically tracked by the radar system. Shows UNKN when not known and ANON when the flight is marked anonymized.
stdds.flight_id.mode_3_a_code: The 4 digit octal Mode 3/A transponder code, automatically tracked. Shows ANON when the flight is marked anonymized.
stdds.slc.coast_num: An internal table index the radar system uses while this track is coasting (temporarily not being freshly updated by a sensor).
stdds.slc.local_av_num: An internal table index into the airport's local aircraft/vehicle list. Always empty in our data.
stdds.slc.susp_num: An internal table index for a suspended track (one the radar system has temporarily set aside). Always empty in our data.
stdds.manual.ac_type: Aircraft type in ICAO format, entered by hand by an air traffic controller. Shows ANON if the flight is marked anonymized.
stdds.manual.call_num: Callsign entered by hand by an air traffic controller. Shows ANON if the flight is marked anonymized.
stdds.manual.category: Wake turbulence category letter entered by hand by a controller (how much wake turbulence the aircraft generates).
stdds.manual.fix: A paired navigation fix entered by hand by a controller, similar in purpose to flight_info.fix.
stdds.manual.mode_3_a_code: The 4 digit octal Mode 3/A transponder code, entered by hand by a controller. Shows ANON if the flight is marked anonymized.
stdds.manual.scratchpad_1: First line of free-form text a controller typed into the aircraft's data tag, e.g. a note or a gate number. 'none' means no text was entered.
stdds.manual.scratchpad_2: Second line of free-form text a controller typed into the aircraft's data tag, e.g. a runway or taxiway note. 'none' means no text was entered.
stdds.movement: The container for the movement.* fields (acceleration, heading, speed, velocity). It has no value of its own in the flattened table, so it always shows as empty here.

tfms_ti.position_timestamp: The same time as common.position_timestamp below, duplicated at the top level only because BigQuery needs a top-level field to partition the table on; it cannot partition on a field nested inside common. Not separate information.
tfms_ti.simple_altitude: The Flight Level as air traffic control would say it, written as a string like 360C for FL360. The trailing letter says how the altitude was reported: C means the beacon altitude is within the FAA's conformance limit, T means an interim altitude is shown while climbing or descending. Multiply the number by 100 to get feet, which is what feeds common.altitude_ft.
tfms_ti.common.ac_type: Always empty for TFMS. This source does not carry an aircraft type code.
tfms_ti.common.adshex: Always empty for TFMS. TFMS has no ICAO 24-bit address; flights are identified by callsign and flight reference instead.
tfms_ti.common.altitude_ft: Altitude in feet, worked out from simple_altitude times 100 (Flight Level converted to feet). This is a pressure altitude rounded to the nearest 100 ft; at one FAA facility (EUC) the rule is different, multiplying values under 5,000 ft by 10 instead and leaving values at or above 5,000 ft unset.
tfms_ti.common.asi_received_timestamp: The time, in microseconds since the Unix epoch, when ASI's TFMS integration parsed this message into structured form. This is an ASI-side ingest time, not the position time.
tfms_ti.common.callsign: The flight callsign as sent by TFMS. If this comes through empty, ASI's later fusion step fills it in from fltd_message_attributes.acid instead, though that happens downstream of this raw table.
tfms_ti.common.ground_speed_kt: Ground speed in knots, as TFMS reports it for the aircraft.
tfms_ti.common.latitude: Latitude in decimal degrees (WGS84), between -90 and 90. TFMS positions come from radar tracking rather than GPS. In some facilities (seen around Vancouver) they are snapped to a 1 arc-minute grid and sit about 2.3 km from where ADS-B places the same aircraft; in others (seen around Paris) they are precise but about 5 seconds behind.
tfms_ti.common.longitude: Longitude in decimal degrees (WGS84), between -180 and 180. Same accuracy notes as common.latitude apply.
tfms_ti.common.position_timestamp: The time TFMS says the aircraft was at this position, in microseconds since the Unix epoch. TFMS positions typically arrive 5 to 18 seconds after this time.
tfms_ti.common.source_identifier: A numeric code identifying TFMS TI as the source of this plot. The same value for every row here.
tfms_ti.common.source_received_timestamp: For TFMS this is a real, separate timestamp: it comes from the FAA's own sourceTimeStamp field, i.e. when the source facility actually sent the message. Unlike most other sources, where this field just copies position_timestamp, for TFMS it can be used to measure TFMS's own lag.
tfms_ti.common.squawk: Always empty for TFMS. This source does not carry a transponder squawk code.
tfms_ti.common.tail_number: Always empty for TFMS. This source does not carry a registration or tail number.
tfms_ti.common.track_identifier: A synthetic key TFMS builds by combining the flight reference number with the date, so it changes with each flight leg rather than staying fixed to one aircraft the way an ICAO address would.
tfms_ti.fltd_message_attributes.acid: The aircraft ID the FAA's TFMS uses for this flight: either a callsign or a tail number, whichever TFMS has on file. ASI's fusion step uses this to fill in the callsign when common.callsign is empty.
tfms_ti.fltd_message_attributes.airline: The three-letter airline code for the flight, such as DAL for Delta. XXX means the flight has no airline, for example general aviation.
tfms_ti.fltd_message_attributes.arr_arpt: The arrival airport for this flight, as TFMS knows it. May or may not be an ICAO code, and can be empty if not yet known.
tfms_ti.fltd_message_attributes.cdm_part: Whether this flight belongs to a Collaborative Decision Making participant, meaning an airline or operator that shares real-time schedule data with the FAA. Stored as the text true or false rather than a real boolean.
tfms_ti.fltd_message_attributes.dep_arpt: The departure airport for this flight, as TFMS knows it. May or may not be an ICAO code, and can be empty if not yet known.
tfms_ti.fltd_message_attributes.flight_ref: The FAA's internal reference number for this flight, unique for roughly a few months. Combined with the date to build common.track_identifier.
tfms_ti.fltd_message_attributes.major: A carrier code for the flight: a real three-letter airline code, a TFMS-only placeholder starting with a period, a filtered four-letter code, or XXX if none of those apply.
tfms_ti.fltd_message_attributes.sensitivity: How restricted this data is for distribution. R means government agencies only, A means everyone including government, D means everyone except government, to avoid duplicates.
tfms_ti.fltd_message_attributes.source_facility: The FAA facility or system that sent this message, such as KZDV or KZLC, an air route traffic control center.
tfms_ti.fltd_message_attributes.source_timestamp: The time the source facility sent the message that produced this data, in microseconds since the Unix epoch. This is the accurate send time for TFMS and matches common.source_received_timestamp.
tfms_ti.qualified_aircraft_id.aircraft_category: A broad aircraft category: JET, TURBO (turboprop), PROP, PISTON, or OTHER. Only JET, TURBO and PROP are documented; PISTON and OTHER show up in the data anyway.
tfms_ti.qualified_aircraft_id.aircraft_id: The same aircraft ID as fltd_message_attributes.acid (a callsign or tail number), repeated here.
tfms_ti.qualified_aircraft_id.arrival_point__air: The arrival airport. Looks like a duplicate of fltd_message_attributes.arr_arpt; kept as a separate field until that is confirmed.
tfms_ti.qualified_aircraft_id.computer_id__facil: The FAA facility handling this flight. Looks like a duplicate of fltd_message_attributes.source_facility; kept as a separate field until that is confirmed.
tfms_ti.qualified_aircraft_id.computer_id__id_nu: The FAA's internal computer ID number for this flight within its facility, such as FFF or 374. Unclear exactly how this differs from flight_ref.
tfms_ti.qualified_aircraft_id.departure_point__a: The departure airport. Looks like a duplicate of fltd_message_attributes.dep_arpt; kept as a separate field until that is confirmed.
tfms_ti.qualified_aircraft_id.gufi: The Global Unique Flight Identifier: a 10-character code, where the first character is an ICAO country code, the second is a facility letter, and the last eight identify the flight. Often empty in our data.
tfms_ti.qualified_aircraft_id.user_category: The type of operator flying this aircraft: AIR_TAXI, CARGO, COMMERCIAL, GENERAL_AVIATION (sometimes written with a space instead of an underscore), MILITARY, or OTHER.

ual.air_temperature: This is the outside air temperature as United sends it, for example M46 for minus 46. Probably degrees Celsius, matching the format Alaska uses for static_air_temp, but United does not label the unit.
ual.airline_code_cid: This is United's internal numeric code for the airline, used as part of the flight key. It is constant here because every row is a United flight.
ual.airline_code_iata: This is the 2-letter airline code, UA for United. It is constant here because every row is a United flight.
ual.airline_code_icao: This is the 3-letter airline code, UAL for United. It is constant here because every row is a United flight.
ual.altitude: This is the flight level United reports, so 350 means flight level 350, roughly 35000 feet. Multiply by 100 to get feet, which is exactly how common.altitude_ft is worked out.
ual.arrival_icao: This is the destination airport's 4-letter ICAO code, like KSFO.
ual.dispatch_desk: This names the dispatch desk handling the flight. It is empty in every row we have.
ual.flight_leg_instance_number: This counts repeated legs for the same flight number on the same day. It is 0 in every row we have.
ual.flight_number: This is the flight number United uses, like 1960.
ual.fuel: This is the fuel on board. Probably pounds, since the values line up with the pounds-based total_fuel_lbs field on the Alaska side, but United does not label the unit.
ual.interface_version: This is the version number of the message format United sends. It is constant here.
ual.position: This is the raw position string United sends, like N39263W106539. It packs latitude and longitude together as degrees and minutes; common.latitude and common.longitude are worked out from it.
ual.report_datetime: This is when United's system created this position report, shown as a date and time. It is the report key, paired with the position.
ual.sched_dep_date_time: This is the flight's scheduled departure date and time.
ual.sched_dep_icao: This is the scheduled departure airport's 4-letter ICAO code, like KLAS.
ual.source_timestamp: This is the timestamp United puts on the message, shown as a date and time. It feeds both this field and common.position_timestamp.
ual.speed: This is the aircraft's speed in knots. It is optional and only set on 4 of the 15 rows we have.
ual.stub_flight_number: This is meant to hold a placeholder flight number for a flight that has not been assigned a real one yet. It is empty in every row we have.
ual.system_seq_number: This is a sequence number United assigns to the message, used to tell messages apart. It looks like a date and time packed together with a counter, for example 260921155046879 for 2026-09-21 15:50:46.
ual.tail_number: This is the aircraft's registration number, like N2737U, exactly as United sent it, before common.tail_number cleans it up.
ual.wind: This is the wind United reports, direction and speed packed together as digits, for example 273051. Probably 3 digits of direction in degrees followed by speed in knots, the same layout Alaska uses for actual_wind, though the digit count varies from row to row here.
ual.common.ac_type: This holds the aircraft type code, like B738. It is always empty here because neither Alaska nor United sends aircraft type.
ual.common.adshex: This is the ICAO 24-bit address in hex, like A12345. It is always empty here because neither Alaska nor United sends this address.
ual.common.altitude_ft: This is altitude in feet. For United it comes from the flight level times 100, and for Alaska it comes from present_altitude times 100. Both are pressure altitude, not height above the ground.
ual.common.asi_received_timestamp: This is the time our system parsed the message, shown as a date and time. It is set automatically when the integration receives the message, not sent by the airline.
ual.common.callsign: This is the flight callsign, like UAL1960. United builds it from the airline code and flight number, but Alaska never fills it in, so it is always empty for Alaska.
ual.common.ground_speed_kt: This is ground speed in knots. For United it only has a value on 4 of the 15 rows here because the source speed field is optional and often missing.
ual.common.latitude: This is the aircraft's latitude in decimal degrees, worked out from the raw position string the airline sent.
ual.common.longitude: This is the aircraft's longitude in decimal degrees, worked out from the raw position string the airline sent.
ual.common.position_timestamp: This is the time the aircraft was at this position, shown as a date and time. For United it comes from source_timestamp; for Alaska it is built from current_time's date and the more precise system_time.
ual.common.source_identifier: This is a fixed code identifying the source. It never changes within one source's data, since each source only ever reports its own code.
ual.common.source_received_timestamp: This is when the upstream system logged the message, shown as a date and time. For United it comes from report_datetime; for Alaska it comes from current_time.
ual.common.squawk: This is the 4-digit transponder code. It is always empty here because neither Alaska nor United sends a squawk code.
ual.common.tail_number: This is the aircraft's registration number, like N58101, cleaned up into a standard format.
ual.common.track_identifier: This is the ID used to tell aircraft apart within one source. For both United and Alaska it is just the raw tail number, before the cleanup that common.tail_number applies.

uavionix.air_speed: Air speed from the aircraft's own instruments, either indicated airspeed in knots or a Mach number depending on a flag inside the same item (Data Item I021/150). Always empty in our data; not sent by our uAvionix ground stations.
uavionix.barometric_vertical_rate: Rate of climb or descent computed from barometric altitude, in feet per minute (Data Item I021/155). Always empty in our data; not sent by our uAvionix ground stations.
uavionix.emitter_category: What kind of aircraft or vehicle sent the report, as a number the transponder sets (Data Item I021/020): 1 is no category given, 2 to 6 are aircraft sizes from light to heavy, higher numbers cover rotorcraft, gliders, lighter-than-air, unmanned aircraft and ground vehicles. Our data has mostly light, small and medium aircraft.
uavionix.flight_level: Barometric (pressure) altitude from the aircraft's altimeter, in flight levels, so hundreds of feet: 350.0 means FL350, 35,000 ft (Data Item I021/145). The integration writes this times 100 into common.altitude_ft and common.mean_sea_level_altitude_ft since the fix of 22 September (#113, TS-1927); before that, common.altitude_ft used geometric_height instead.
uavionix.geometric_height: Height from the aircraft's own GPS, in feet, measured from the WGS-84 ellipsoid rather than sea level or air pressure (Data Item I021/140). Before 22 September this fed common.altitude_ft; since the fix it feeds nothing downstream, so it now differs from the shared altitude field by the GPS-versus-barometric gap, which runs from a couple hundred feet near the ground to a couple thousand feet at cruise.
uavionix.geometric_vertical_rate: Rate of climb or descent computed from GPS height, in feet per minute (Data Item I021/157). Always empty in our data; not sent by our uAvionix ground stations.
uavionix.magnetic_heading: Heading in degrees, measured from magnetic north rather than true north (Data Item I021/152). Copied straight into common.heading_deg, so that shared field is magnetic for uAvionix but true north for ADS-B Exchange; the two will differ by the local magnetic declination. Only set on about 1 in 90 of our plots.
uavionix.mode_3_a_code: The 4-digit transponder squawk code the pilot dialled in (Mode 3/A), stored here as a plain decimal number rather than as octal digits (Data Item I021/070). The integration formats it back into 4 octal digits for common.squawk; for example 640 here becomes '1200' in common.squawk.
uavionix.position_timestamp: When the aircraft was at this position, as Unix epoch microseconds. Computed from time_message_reception_position (seconds since midnight UTC) mapped onto today's or yesterday's date; identical to common.position_timestamp, since the integration sets both from the same computed value.
uavionix.target_address: The aircraft's 24-bit ICAO address, as a plain decimal number rather than hex (Data Item I021/080). The integration formats it as 6 hex digits for both common.adshex and common.track_identifier, so those two fields are always equal for uAvionix plots.
uavionix.target_identification: The callsign the aircraft's transponder sends, up to 8 characters, sometimes with a trailing '?' for an unset character slot (Data Item I021/170).
