Copied into common.callsign after trimming whitespace and any trailing '?', but only kept when the result is 1 to 8 characters and has at least one letter; many general-aviation aircraft here send their tail number (e.g. N115UV) as this field, since they have no flight number, and a value that is all digits (e.g. '1200') fails the letter check and leaves common.callsign empty.
uavionix.time_message_reception_position: Seconds since midnight UTC when the uAvionix ground station received the position message (Data Item I021/073). The integration converts this into an absolute timestamp for position_timestamp, common.position_timestamp and common.source_received_timestamp, so all three trace back to this one value; there is no separate upstream-ingest time for this source.
uavionix.time_message_reception_velocity: Seconds since midnight UTC when the ground station received the velocity part of the message (Data Item I021/075). Parsed into the message but not used anywhere else in the uAvionix integration. Set on almost every plot in our data.
uavionix.time_of_report_transmission: Seconds since midnight UTC when the ground station's ASTERIX report was transmitted onward (Data Item I021/077). Parsed into the message but not used anywhere else in the uAvionix integration.
uavionix.true_airspeed: The whole true airspeed item (Data Item I021/151): whether the value exceeds the item's range, plus the true airspeed itself in knots (see true_airspeed.true_airspeed). Always empty as its own column in our data; not sent by our uAvionix ground stations.
uavionix.airborne_ground_vector.ground_speed: Ground speed from the aircraft's own GPS-derived velocity, in nautical miles per second, the ASTERIX unit (Data Item I021/160, 2^-14 NM/s steps). Before the fix of 22 September (#114) this raw value was copied unchanged into common.ground_speed_kt, making every uAvionix speed 3,600 times too small; since the fix, common.ground_speed_kt is this value times 3600.
uavionix.airborne_ground_vector.is_range_exceeded: True when the ground speed above is outside the item's defined range and should not be trusted. False on every plot in our data.
uavionix.airborne_ground_vector.track_angle: Track over the ground in degrees, true north (Data Item I021/160). Copied straight into common.track_deg, so common.track_deg is only set on the roughly two thirds of plots that carry this item.
uavionix.aircraft_operational_status.has_single_a: Whether the aircraft's transponder has only one antenna instead of the usual two, part of Data Item I021/008. Always empty in our data.
uavionix.aircraft_operational_status.is_capable_o: Whether the aircraft can generate Air-Referenced Velocity (ARV) reports, part of Data Item I021/008. Always empty in our data.
Whether the aircraft can send Target State reports, part of Data Item I021/008. Always empty in our data.
uavionix.aircraft_operational_status.is_cdti_oper: Whether the pilot's Cockpit Display of Traffic Information (CDTI) is working, part of Data Item I021/008. Always empty in our data.
uavionix.aircraft_operational_status.is_tcas_not_: Whether the aircraft's Traffic Collision Avoidance System (TCAS) is switched off or not working, part of Data Item I021/008. Set on every plot in our data, mostly false.
uavionix.aircraft_operational_status.is_tcas_reso: Whether TCAS currently has an active resolution advisory, telling the pilot to climb or descend to avoid a collision, part of Data Item I021/008. False on every plot in our data.
uavionix.aircraft_operational_status.target_tc_re: Whether the aircraft can send Trajectory Change (TC) reports, and how many at once, part of Data Item I021/008. Always empty in our data.
uavionix.common.above_ground_altitude_ft: Height above the ground terrain directly below, in feet. Not set by the uAvionix integration; the multiplexer computes it downstream from common.altitude_ft and a terrain map. Always empty in this raw table. Fusion treats a missing value here as 'presumed airborne', which matters for uAvionix since it does not always fill altitude_ft either.
uavionix.common.ac_type: ICAO aircraft type code, for example B738. Always empty for uAvionix; this source does not carry aircraft type.
uavionix.common.adshex: ICAO 24-bit address in hex, formatted here from target_address. Equal to common.track_identifier for uAvionix plots.
uavionix.common.altitude_ft: Altitude in feet, uAvionix's version of the shared altitude field used across all sources. Since the fix of 22 September (#113, TS-1927) this is flight_level times 100, the barometric pressure altitude, falling back to 0 when the aircraft's ground bit is set and no flight level is present. Before the fix it preferred geometric_height (GPS height) instead, which runs hundreds to thousands of feet higher than barometric altitude at cruise, so any analysis on data from before 22 September should treat this field as GPS height, not barometric altitude.
uavionix.common.asi_received_timestamp: Unix epoch microseconds, when the uAvionix integration parsed this plot into structured form. Set from the wall clock at parse time, not from anything in the ASTERIX message itself.
uavionix.common.callsign: Aircraft callsign, taken from target_identification after trimming whitespace and a trailing '?', kept only if the result has 1 to 8 characters and at least one letter. Empty when target_identification is missing or fails that check, for example when it holds only digits.
uavionix.common.flight_number: Flight number, for example AAL1234. Always empty for uAvionix; only PlaneFinder fills this shared field.
uavionix.common.ground_speed_kt: Ground speed in knots, the shared field used across all sources. Since the fix of 22 September (#114) this is airborne_ground_vector.ground_speed times 3600, converting from NM/s to knots; before the fix the raw NM/s value was copied in unconverted, so every uAvionix ground speed here was 3,600 times too small.
uavionix.common.heading_deg: Heading in degrees, copied from magnetic_heading. Unlike ADS-B Exchange, which reports true heading in this shared field, uAvionix reports magnetic heading here, so the two sources disagree by the local magnetic declination. Only set on about 1% of plots.
uavionix.common.latitude: WGS84 latitude in decimal degrees, taken from high_resolution_position when present, otherwise the coarser position field.
uavionix.common.longitude: WGS84 longitude in decimal degrees, same fallback as latitude: high_resolution_position first, then the coarser position field.
uavionix.common.mean_sea_level_altitude_ft: Altitude in feet, meant to be true height above sea level. For most sources this shared field is computed downstream by the multiplexer, not by the source integration, but uAvionix is an exception: its own integration sets this directly to flight_level times 100, the same barometric altitude as common.altitude_ft since the fix of 22 September. The multiplexer still overwrites it again further downstream using its own formula from altitude_ft, so this raw value only reflects what uAvionix itself sent, not the final production value.
uavionix.common.position_timestamp: Unix epoch microseconds, when the aircraft was at this position. Computed from time_message_reception_position; identical to the top-level position_timestamp field.
uavionix.common.provider_source_type: Sub-feed or sensor code within the source. Not set by uAvionix; always 0.
uavionix.common.source_identifier: Which upstream source produced this plot, as the PlotSource enum. Always uAvionix's fixed code (11, UAVIONIX_FLIGHT_LINE) here, since this table only holds uAvionix plots.
uavionix.common.source_received_timestamp: Unix epoch microseconds, meant to be when the upstream system received the position. uAvionix does not expose this separately, so the integration sets it equal to common.position_timestamp; do not use it to estimate upstream-to-ASI lag for this source.
uavionix.common.squawk: 4-digit octal Mode A transponder code, formatted from mode_3_a_code. Example: mode_3_a_code 640 becomes squawk '1200'.
uavionix.common.tail_number: Aircraft registration, for example N12345. Always empty for uAvionix, even though many of its aircraft broadcast a tail-number-like string (e.g. N115UV); that string ends up in common.callsign instead, since uAvionix has no separate registration field.
uavionix.common.track_deg: Track over the ground in degrees, true north, copied from airborne_ground_vector.track_angle. Only set on plots that carry that item, about two thirds of our data.
uavionix.common.track_identifier: Source-specific identifier of the object, formatted from target_address as 6 hex digits. Equal to common.adshex for uAvionix plots.
uavionix.data_source_identification.system_area_c: Which geographic area the reporting ground station belongs to (Data Item I021/010). Constant in our data, since all our uAvionix plots come from the same feed configuration.
uavionix.data_source_identification.system_identi: Which specific ground station or sensor sent the report (Data Item I021/010). Constant in our data, for the same reason as system_area_code.
uavionix.high_resolution_position.latitude: Higher-precision WGS84 latitude in decimal degrees (Data Item I021/131). Preferred over the coarser position.latitude field when building common.latitude, and set on every plot in our data.
uavionix.high_resolution_position.longitude: Higher-precision WGS84 longitude in decimal degrees (Data Item I021/131). Preferred over the coarser position.longitude field when building common.longitude, and set on every plot in our data.
uavionix.mops_version.is_mops_version_not_support: Whether the aircraft's transponder could not report which ADS-B standard version it uses (Data Item I021/210). False on every plot in our data.
uavionix.mops_version.link_technology: Which radio link technology carried the message: other, UAT, 1090ES or VDL Mode 4 (Data Item I021/210). Always empty in our data.
uavionix.mops_version.mops_version: Which version of the ADS-B Minimum Operational Performance Standards (MOPS) the aircraft's transponder follows (Data Item I021/210): 1 is the oldest generation DO-260, 3 is DO-260B, 4 the newest DO-260C. Our data has a mix of DO-260 and DO-260B transponders.
uavionix.position.latitude: WGS84 latitude in decimal degrees, the coarser-resolution position item (Data Item I021/130). Only used to build common.latitude when high_resolution_position is missing.
uavionix.position.longitude: WGS84 longitude in decimal degrees, the coarser-resolution position item (Data Item I021/130). Only used to build common.longitude when high_resolution_position is missing.
uavionix.quality_indicators.geometric_vertical_ac: Geometric Vertical Accuracy (GVA): how confident the aircraft is in the accuracy of its GPS height, as a small number where higher is better. Set on every plot in our data.
uavionix.quality_indicators.is_sil_measured_per_s: Whether the Source Integrity Level (SIL) below was measured per individual sample rather than per hour of operation. False on every plot in our data.
uavionix.quality_indicators.nacp: Navigation Accuracy Category for Position (NACp): how confident the aircraft is in its own GPS position, from 0 (unknown) to 11 (95% of positions within 3 m). Used directly by the harness's Kalman filter and by src/analysis/source_accuracy.py to size the position measurement noise; the Kalman code treats a plot with the ground bit set as having no NACp regardless of this value.
uavionix.quality_indicators.nic_baro: Navigation Integrity Category for barometric altitude (NICbaro): whether the aircraft's barometric altitude has been cross-checked against another source, 1 for cross-checked, 0 for not. Set on every plot in our data.
uavionix.quality_indicators.nucp_or_nic: Navigation Uncertainty Category for Position (older transponders) or Navigation Integrity Category (current standard): a radius the aircraft guarantees its position is within, on a 0 to 11 scale where higher means smaller and better. Read by the harness's server.py and source_accuracy.py as this source's NIC value, the counterpart to nacp.
uavionix.quality_indicators.nucr_or_nacv: Navigation Uncertainty Category for velocity (older transponders) or Navigation Accuracy Category for Velocity (current standard): how accurate the aircraft's own speed estimate is. Read by src/analysis/source_accuracy.py as this source's NACv value.
uavionix.quality_indicators.position_integrity_ca: Position Integrity Category (PIC), a third-extension field of Data Item I021/090. Always empty in our data.
uavionix.quality_indicators.sil: Source Integrity Level (SIL): how confident the aircraft is that its NIC guarantee is actually met, on a 0 to 3 scale where higher is more confident. Set on every plot in our data.
uavionix.quality_indicators.system_design_assuran: System Design Assurance (SDA): how rigorously the aircraft's ADS-B equipment was designed and tested against failure, on a 0 to 3 scale where higher is more rigorous. Set on every plot in our data.
uavionix.target_report_descriptor.address_type: What kind of address the aircraft's ID is: ICAO (a registered aircraft), duplicate, surface vehicle, or anonymous, part of Data Item I021/040. Always ICAO (1) in our data, meaning every plot is from a normally registered aircraft.
uavionix.target_report_descriptor.altitude_report: Whether the aircraft's altimeter reports in 25 ft or 100 ft steps, or is unknown or invalid, part of Data Item I021/040. Always 25 ft resolution (1) in our data.
uavionix.target_report_descriptor.confidence_leve: Whether the ground station considers this report valid, suspect, or has no information about it, part of Data Item I021/040. Always 'valid' (1) in our data.
uavionix.target_report_descriptor.did_cpr_validat: Whether the aircraft's Compact Position Reporting (CPR) decoding failed a validation check, part of Data Item I021/040. Always empty in our data.
uavionix.target_report_descriptor.did_independent: Whether an independent check of the aircraft's position failed, part of Data Item I021/040. Always empty in our data.
uavionix.target_report_descriptor.did_range_check: Whether the aircraft's report failed a range plausibility check, part of Data Item I021/040. Always empty in our data, not just false.
Whether the aircraft's report passed a range plausibility check, part of Data Item I021/040. True on every plot in our data.
uavionix.target_report_descriptor.has_differentia: Whether the aircraft's position used differential GPS correction, part of Data Item I021/040. False on every plot in our data.
uavionix.target_report_descriptor.is_ground_bit_s: Whether the aircraft itself is signalling that it is on the ground, part of Data Item I021/040. Used by the harness as the on-ground flag for uAvionix: src/harness/viewer/server.py reads it directly for the viewer's on-ground column, and src/harness/strategies/kalman.py drops the plot's altitude when this is true.
uavionix.target_report_descriptor.is_ldpj_detecte: Whether a Local Decoding Position Jump (a sudden implausible position jump the ground station caught) was detected, part of Data Item I021/040. Always empty in our data.
uavionix.target_report_descriptor.is_nogo_bit_set: Whether the aircraft's navigation system has flagged itself as unfit for use ('NoGo'), part of Data Item I021/040. Always empty in our data.
uavionix.target_report_descriptor.is_not_capable_: Whether the aircraft cannot report the pilot's selected altitude, part of Data Item I021/040. False on every plot in our data.
uavionix.target_report_descriptor.is_report_from_: Whether this report came from a field monitor rather than the aircraft's own transponder, part of Data Item I021/040. False on every plot in our data.
uavionix.target_report_descriptor.is_simulated_ta: Whether this is a simulated target rather than a real aircraft, part of Data Item I021/040. False on every plot in our data.
uavionix.target_report_descriptor.is_target_suspe: Whether the ground station flags this target's report as suspect, part of Data Item I021/040. Always empty in our data.
uavionix.target_report_descriptor.is_test_target: Whether this is a test target rather than a real aircraft, part of Data Item I021/040. False on every plot in our data.
uavionix.target_report_descriptor.maximum_bits_co: The largest number of bits the ground station corrected while decoding this message, part of Data Item I021/040. Always empty in our data.
uavionix.target_report_descriptor.total_bits_corr: Total number of bits the ground station corrected while decoding this message, part of Data Item I021/040. Always empty in our data.
uavionix.target_status.is_intent_change_active: Whether the aircraft's flight intent, such as its route or altitude plan, has recently changed, part of Data Item I021/200. False on every plot in our data.
uavionix.target_status.is_military_emergency: Whether the aircraft is signalling a military emergency, part of Data Item I021/200. False on every plot in our data.
uavionix.target_status.is_not_lateral_navigation_: Whether the aircraft's lateral navigation (autopilot flying a planned route) is switched off, part of Data Item I021/200. Unclear: true on every single plot in our data across 378 aircraft, which may mean none of them had it engaged, or that this bit defaults to 'not engaged' whenever the aircraft does not actively report the opposite.
uavionix.target_status.priority_status: What kind of emergency the aircraft is declaring, if any: general emergency, medical emergency, minimum fuel, no communications, unlawful interference or downed aircraft, part of Data Item I021/200. Always 'none' (0) in our data.
uavionix.target_status.surveillance_status: Special surveillance condition the aircraft is in: permanent alert, temporary alert, or the pilot's ident (SPI) button pressed, part of Data Item I021/200. Our data has a mix of normal, temporary alert and ident-pressed plots.
uavionix.airborne_ground_vector: The whole airborne ground vector item (Data Item I021/160): ground speed, track angle, and whether either exceeds the item's range. Always empty as its own column in our data; the real values are the separate airborne_ground_vector.* fields.
uavionix.true_airspeed.is_range_exceeded: Whether the true airspeed below is outside the item's defined range, part of Data Item I021/151. Always empty in our data.
uavionix.true_airspeed.true_airspeed: True airspeed in knots, the aircraft's speed through the air rather than over the ground, part of Data Item I021/151. Always empty in our data; not sent by our uAvionix ground stations.
